adjudication_label: batch_9:Synergistic FCC-HCP transformation and TRIP effect comparison
canonical_question: How does the 'synergistic FCC-HCP martensitic transformation' referenced in Figure 5 b,c differ from the standard TRIP effect in bulk materials?

question_variants.question: How does the 'synergistic FCC-HCP martensitic transformation' referenced in Figure 5 b,c differ from the standard TRIP effect in bulk materials?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text describes the synergistic FCC-HCP martensitic transformation in CoNiCrFeMn nanowires and links it to temperature-dependent deformation and Figure 5b,c. However, it does not provide a comparative analysis distinguishing this specific nanowire transformation from the standard TRIP effect in bulk materials.

answers.answer: Partial dislocation nucleation promotes temperature-dependent synergistic FCC-HCP martensitic transformation during later stages of tensile deformation. The text does not explicitly compare this to the standard bulk TRIP effect.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison data provided against bulk materials
evidence_spans: In high entropy alloy (HEA) CoNiCrFeMn nanowires, the motion of the partial dislocation is hindered by the friction due to difference in the lattice parameter of the constituent atoms which is responsible for the hardening and lowering the ductility.
In this study, we have examined the temperature-dependent superplasticity of single component Ag and multicomponent CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires using molecular dynamics simulations.
The results demonstrate that Ag nanowires exhibit apparent temperature-dependent superplasticity at cryogenic temperature due to (110) to (100) cross-section reorientation behavior.

source_evidence_spans: Thus, partial dislocation nucleation also promotes temperature-dependent synergistic FCC-HCP martensitic transformation during later stages of tensile deformation as seen in Figure 5 b,c.
